title: This Battery Runs on Salt—and It Just Matched Tesla's Power!
summary: What if your next electric car ran on salt? Not table salt, but sodium—a metal that's super common and cheap. A Chinese company called Hina has built a sodium-ion battery, and when scientists put it through tough tests, they got a big surprise. It performed almost as well as Tesla's famous lithium-ion batteries! Lithium is rare and expensive, and mining it can hurt the environment. Sodium, on the other hand, is everywhere—in seawater, for example. So a battery that uses sodium could cost a lot less and be easier to make. But could it really match the power and quality of a top lithium battery? To find out, researchers tested 120 Hina cells. They measured how evenly each cell was made, then pushed them hard at different temperatures—from freezing cold to scorching hot. They even used X-rays to peek inside without breaking them open. The results? 'We were positively surprised by how uniform the cells are,' said researcher Moritz Schütte. The battery's design even copies a clever trick from Tesla: a tabless, double-aluminum current collector that cuts resistance and spreads heat evenly. The sodium battery handled high power well and worked great in the cold—except when charging below freezing. That's a weakness they need to fix. Also, its energy density (how much power it packs for its size) is still lower than the best lithium cells. But for things like storing solar energy for a building or powering a city bus that doesn't need to go super far, this could be a game-changer. As Schütte said, 'It will be exciting to see future sodium-ion technologies that are free of nickel and copper, too.' The age of salt-powered batteries might be closer than you think!
why_it_matters: If salt-based batteries become common, electric cars and solar power storage could become cheaper and better for the planet, which affects the world you’ll grow up in.

keywords.explanation: A type of battery that uses sodium (a common metal) instead of rare lithium to store energy.
The most common type of rechargeable battery, found in phones, laptops, and electric cars.
How much power a battery can hold compared to its size or weight.
A part inside a battery that helps electricity flow in and out with less resistance.
A clever design without extra metal tabs that makes a battery handle high power and heat more evenly.
When all battery cells are made so evenly that they perform almost exactly the same.

background_read: Lithium-ion batteries power almost all our gadgets, but lithium is mined mostly in a few countries and can cause pollution.
Sodium is one of the most common elements on Earth — it’s found in ordinary salt and sea water, so it’s much cheaper and easier to get.
Tesla, the famous electric car company, has been pushing battery technology forward for years with clever designs like the tabless current collector.
Article_Structure: WHO: Researchers testing a sodium-ion battery made by Chinese company Hina
WHAT: Ran tough tests on 120 cells and found they performed almost as well as Tesla’s best lithium batteries
WHERE: In a laboratory, using X-rays and tests at different temperatures
WHY: To see if cheap, common sodium could replace lithium and make electric cars and energy storage cleaner and more affordable

perspectives.description: Fans of this technology say it could make batteries much cheaper and reduce the environmental damage of mining rare metals like lithium and nickel.
Sodium batteries still can’t pack as much power into the same space as the very best lithium cells, so they won’t replace lithium in long-range electric cars just yet.
